narrative.overview: Direction decided: the app is moving to muted sage green, and the Login page is the first surface built in it. The app should feel like sitting down at your own kitchen table on payday with a notepad and a calculator: personal, unhurried and approachable, never corporate or bank-like. It's your money in your words ("bucket", "leftover", "covered"), laid out so you can see the whole paycheck at a glance and trust the arithmetic without checking it twice. The visual system is mid-redesign: the Budget Categories page is the reference for the new direction, and older pages move toward it as they're touched. The warmth comes from plain language, generous spacing, and copy that talks to you, not from invented warm colors or decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Light gray page (`page`) with white panels; one accent at a time on any given page
Lists of rows (name on the left, money input on the right), not one card per item
Money always in tabular figures, right-aligned, with a muted `$` sign
The result of every calculation is visible without scrolling (a pinned panel, or a bottom bar on narrow screens)
Plain-language states for good and bad outcomes ("Over budget by", "Every dollar is assigned")

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each page uses exactly one accent color. Red appears only when something is actually wrong.

rules.name: The Words-Not-Just-Red Rule
rules.body: A bad state always changes the label too ("Over budget by $42.10"), not just the color.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every money value uses tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) and lines up on the right, so columns of amounts can be scanned.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case ("Pre-tax benefits"). The older uppercase, letter-spaced micro-labels ("POSTED", "AMOUNT PER PAYCHECK") are legacy and shouldn't be copied into new work.

rules.name: The Zoom-Proof Rule
rules.body: No layout styles (flex centering, `height: 100vh`) on `body` or `#root`, and no hardcoded navbar offsets. Every page must stay fully reachable at 200% zoom.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the thing is above the page: pinned, dragged or open. Shadows don't signal hover. The older zero-offset blue hover glow (`0 0 8px rgb(0,140,255)`) is legacy and shouldn't spread.

dos: Do take color, display type, and the field-and-card treatment from the Login page, and working-page structure from Budget Categories.
Do follow the Budget Categories page for new or redesigned pages: rows inside one list, money inputs, results pinned beside the work.
Do use tabular figures and right-alignment for every money value.
Do say the state in words ("Over budget by $42.10", "Every dollar is assigned") as well as with color.
Do prefix page-specific CSS classes (for example `bc-`). Create React App loads every stylesheet on every page, so unprefixed names like `.drag-handle` leak between pages.
Do check every page at 200% zoom and below 900px wide.
Do use inline SVG icons (grip, close, chevron) in one consistent stroke.
donts: Don't introduce new purple or blue. New and redesigned surfaces use sage. Don't mix sage with a legacy accent on one page.
Don't put layout styles on `body`/`#root`, or offset content by a hardcoded navbar height.
Don't add gradients, zero-offset glow shadows, or uppercase letter-spaced micro-labels to new work. They're legacy.
Don't use one card per item for lists of amounts. Use rows in a single list.
Don't use test amber anywhere except the test instance's indicators.
Don't put real financial figures in screenshots, fixtures or examples. Use mock numbers.
